# Concurrency & performance development notes

> Threads, RunLoop, keeping a thread alive, UI stalls and performance investigation.

## Historical context

Historical development notes from 2015–2017. Their original publication dates and source attribution are retained; translation or catalog updates do not make the examples current.
The examples were not rerun for this reorganization. Old Swift syntax, APIs, dependencies, service addresses and App Store rules may be obsolete; check current official documentation before applying them.

## Articles by original publication date

- [Bison's guide to iOS multithreading, part 1](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-01-13-bison-s-guide-to-ios-multithreading-part-1/index.md): Introduces multithreading by distinguishing processes from threads and comparing NSThread, NSOperationQueue and GCD. It then demonstrates thread creation, execution, termination and priorities, using logs to observe scheduling behaviour. Originally published: 2016-01-13. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Bison's guide to iOS multithreading, part 2](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-01-18-bison-s-guide-to-ios-multithreading-part-2/index.md): Examines shared data accessed by several threads, introducing synchronized blocks and NSLock locking and unlocking. NSCondition examples then use waiting, signalling and broadcasting to explain coordination between threads. Originally published: 2016-01-18. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Bison's guide to iOS multithreading, part 3](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-02-29-bison-s-guide-to-ios-multithreading-part-3/index.md): Explores GCD tasks and queues, comparing the main queue, global queues and custom serial and concurrent queues. Image downloads, repeated execution and one-time initialisation illustrate common ways to submit work. Originally published: 2016-02-29. Published in 2016, using the Objective-C GCD interfaces. Some conceptual statements in the body need to be checked against the code. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [UIKit performance tuning in practice](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-03-02-uikit-performance-tuning-in-practice/index.md): Uses a list interface as an experiment and Instruments' Core Animation tools to examine layer blending, image dimensions, colour formats and offscreen rendering. It connects common scrolling-performance problems with targeted adjustments. Originally published: 2016-03-02. Published in 2016. Interpret the debugging interface, refresh-rate examples and rendering conclusions in the context of that environment. Originally credited to bestswifter; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Optimising UITableViewCell height calculation in Swift](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-04-25-optimising-uitableviewcell-height-calculation-in-swift/index.md): Addresses repeated cell-height calculation by drawing on FDTemplateLayoutCell's template measurement and height-caching approach. A Swift wrapper reduces repeated work during table-view scrolling. Originally published: 2016-04-25. Published in 2016. The Swift implementation uses the list-layout and caching interfaces available then. Originally credited to 大石头布; edited and archived by Bison.
- [RunLoop and Keeping iOS Threads Alive](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-07-26-runloop-and-keeping-ios-threads-alive/index.md): Uses the networking thread in AFNetworking 2.x to examine RunLoop-based thread lifetimes. It explains how copied run-loop code can retain objects or prevent threads from exiting, then explores more controlled lifecycle handling through examples. Originally published: 2016-07-26. The article specifically examines the NSURLConnection networking thread implementation in AFNetworking 2.x. Originally credited to bestswifter; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Detecting iOS Main-Thread Stalls](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-03-27-detecting-ios-main-thread-stalls/index.md): Detects stalls by monitoring the main thread's RunLoop state and wait timeouts. It then introduces retrieving thread stack frames, walking call stacks, and symbolication to capture useful diagnostic context while an app is running. Originally published: 2017-03-27. Published in 2017, the stack-reading and symbolication code reflects the operating systems and processor architectures of that period. Originally credited to SindriLin; edited and archived by Bison.
